tagline: Alaska's oldest highway, from the bison country to Santa's door.
intro: The north end of the Richardson comes up through Delta Junction, where the Alaska Highway runs out, and heads on north for Fairbanks. The road began in 1898 as an Army pack trail to Eagle, an all-American route to the Klondike gold fields. After the Fairbanks strike it was made a wagon road under Wilds P. Richardson, opened to automobiles in the 1920s and paved in 1957.
Roadhouses stood along the old trail about every 15 to 20 miles. In 1928 a herd of 23 bison was brought up from Montana for the hunters, and it still roams the Delta Junction country.

moments.title: Rika's Roadhouse
moments.text: At the old Tanana crossing, John Hajdukovich deeded his roadhouse to Rika Wallen in place of back wages, and she ran it for many years, even after a bridge downriver drew the traffic off.

moments.title: North Pole
moments.text: The homestead was renamed North Pole in 1952 in hopes of attracting a toy manufacturer, and a trading post opened on the highway that year grew into Santa Claus House, 42-foot Santa and all.
